subject: LaunchPad ramping proposal and per-token step-up schedule
messages:
From: Anna Park <anna@launchpad.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@launchpad.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Launch week ramp plan + ask for per-token pricing

Hi Diego / Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team loved the low-latency routing and the KV cache examples. We have a product launch in Q3 and need help structuring a monthly committed plan that lets us ramp quickly but keeps unit economics predictable. Attached is a short deck with the launch timeline and rough traffic profile (Launch_Ramp_Deck.pdf).

High level ask: can Redwood provide a stepped monthly commit schedule (3 months) with clear per-token discount tiers and true-up rules for seasonality/launch surges? Specifically we want:
- A conservative Month 1 commit (pilot) with an easy step-up for Month 2/3
- A model for temporary surge capacity during launch week
- Clear pricing breakpoints so internal stakeholders can forecast cost if traffic overshoots

Constraints to note:
- We expect heavy bursts the first two weeks post-launch, then stabilization around 60% of peak.
- Regulatory: all data for this launch stays in the US region.

Would you be able to sketch the commit tiers and discount levels, and confirm whether true-ups are monthly or quarterly? Also include any preferred language for SOW / billing timing.

Proposed next step: short call Wednesday to walk numbers.

Thanks,
Anna Park
Head of Product Ops | LaunchPad, Inc.

---
Attachments: Launch_Ramp_Deck.pdf (11 pages)
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Anna Park <anna@launchpad.ai>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Launch week ramp plan + ask for per-token pricing

Thanks Anna — deck looked good. Looping in Rachel (pricing lead) and Vivek (solutions) to make sure we address SLO/surge guardrails.

High-level (sketch):
- Baseline per-token list: $0.00028 / token for hosted generation (context + output tokens combined).
- Step-up commit suggestion (monthly committed usage):
  * Month 1 (Pilot): 400M tokens committed
  * Month 2 (Scale): 1.2B tokens committed
  * Month 3 (Launch steady-state): 2.8B tokens committed
- Discount schedule (applied to baseline unit price once commit tier is met in month):
  * >= 500M tokens: 10% off list
  * >= 1.5B tokens: 18% off list
  * >= 3.0B tokens: 25% off list
- Surge allowance: automatic burst pool up to +30% of committed tokens at a +15% surcharge on the discounted price for that month; separate negotiated carve-outs for launch weeks available (we can grant a one-time larger burst at no surcharge if committed ramp is hit ahead of schedule).
- True-up: monthly true-up recommended (keeps invoicing aligned with usage spikes). Quarterly true-up is possible for larger enterprise contracts but adds reconciliation lag.

Attached is a quick working sheet with the stepped commit numbers and an example invoice calculation (commit_schedule_proposal.xlsx). We kept the first-month commit conservative to reduce runway risk.

Questions for you:
1) Do the commit levels above map to your traffic projections?
2) Do you need a guaranteed burst carve-out (we can pre-approve a launch-week buffer in the SOW)?
3) Any procurement constraints on payment terms (Net 30 vs Net 45)?

We can turn this into an SOW draft after you confirm the commit sizes + surge policy. Happy to join a sync Wed 11am PT.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: commit_schedule_proposal.xlsx (spreadsheet, 3 tabs)
From: Anna Park <anna@launchpad.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@launchpad.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Launch week ramp plan + ask for per-token pricing

Diego — thanks, that framing helps. A few clarifications based on the team review: 

1) Traffic projection: attached is a simple CSV with daily peaks and a 3-month expected shape. The 2.8B month target is our optimistic steady-state; month 2 might be lower at ~1.1B depending on marketing. See traffic_projection.csv.
2) Surge carve-out: yes, we want a guaranteed launch-week buffer. Can Redwood commit to a one-week buffer equal to +100% of Month 3 committed daily average (i.e., temporary capacity doubling) with a capped surcharge (no more than +10% on discounted price) if we hit that? We need the buffer language for our procurement and to commit to a marketing timeline.
3) Payment terms: default is Net 30 but procurement prefers Net 45 for new vendors — we can do Net 30 for the first quarter if Redwood requires faster cadence.

Also: how do you handle rollover unused committed tokens? We prefer a partial rollover (up to 20% of unused commit for the next month) to avoid waste during a launch that fronts loads into the second month.

If you can add explicit SOW language for both the launch-week buffer and partial rollover, procurement can move quickly. Wed 11am PT still good for a quick call.

Thanks,
Anna
---
Attachments: traffic_projection.csv (5KB)
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Anna Park <anna@launchpad.ai>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Launch week ramp plan + ask for per-token pricing

Anna — great notes. Below is the refined position we will include in the SOW draft and invoice schedule. I put conservative language where appropriate to keep procurement comfortable.

Pricing & commit structure (final draft for review):
- Baseline list: $0.00028 / token. Monthly discounts apply against list when commit thresholds are reached for that month.
- Committed monthly schedule (example): Month1: 400M, Month2: 1.1B, Month3: 2.8B. (We will accept your updated Month2 projection of 1.1B.)
- Discount breakpoints: >=500M → 10%, >=1.5B → 18%, >=3.0B → 25%. Discounts apply only to tokens within the month after commit is met.
- Launch-week guaranteed buffer: Redwood will pre-approve a one-week buffer equal to 100% of Month3 daily average (temporary capacity doubling). Buffer pricing: capped surcharge of +10% on the month’s discounted price. If buffer exceeds pre-approved limit we fall back to the standard surge policy (+15% surcharge).
- Rollover: up to 20% of unused committed tokens may roll into the immediately following month (must be used within that month). Rollover cannot be banked beyond one month.
- True-up & billing cadence: monthly true-up with invoice issued on the 5th calendar day after month close; Net 30 payment terms by default (we can accept Net 45 for the first quarter on request).
- SLA & region: commitments and burst guardrails apply to US-hosted capacity only; we’ll document latency SLOs in the SOW appendix.

Next steps:
1) I’ll drop an SOW draft that includes the above language plus the LaunchPad traffic appendix — expect that by EOD tomorrow (SOW_draft.pdf).
2) HubSpot deal update: I linked the proposed commit to HS-82315 so your ops team can see revised pricing.
3) If procurement approves the Net 45 trial for Q1, flag it and we’ll adjust terms in the SOW.

Call confirmed: Wed 11am PT — Diego / Rachel / Vivek will attend to walk the SOW and the DocuSign flow.

Cheers,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: SOW_draft.pdf (6 pages)
